The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 12.01.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-67-E-8750 proceeding on Chikkanahalli Gate, Kolar to Bangalore NH-75 Road, Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote,
Bangalore, at that time a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HT- 9730 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to the forced impact, petitioner and rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 32 years, the petitioner was working as Carpenter and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court and he remained placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition.

Further this respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending Manjunatha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 20 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2854192/
2 motorcycle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: Further this respondent submits that, the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-67-E-8750 was not holding valid and effective driving license to ride the vehicle as on the date of accident and taken 2 persons as pillion riders and caused accident by himself.
It is further submitted that, accident was due to rash and negligence of both the motorcyclists and both of them involved in the accident and it is a contributory negligence.
Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.

By these reasons,
it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HT-9730 on 12.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., near Chikkanahalli Gate, Kolar to Bangalore NH-75 Road,
Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.11 and closed his side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under;

Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
8.

ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 12.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m.,
petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-67-E- 8750 proceeding on Chikkanahalli Gate, Kolar to Bangalore NH-75 Road, Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote, Bangalore, at that time a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HT-9730 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to the forced impact, petitioner and rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Nandagudi Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.09/2024.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HT-9730.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "
The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt,
as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Nandagudi Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 9/2024.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 9 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending motorcycle.

The Ex.P.3 (spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.7, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending Tipper Lorry U/s.
279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.4 & 5 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Reports discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M. V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16.

sentences.text: In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-HT-9730.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.

Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock,
severe pain and sufferings.
18. In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient.
But the petitioner was failed to produced the discharge summary.
Further the petitioner has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6, wherein the doctor has opined that the injuries are grevious in nature.
19. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

In support of his plea, he has produced 03 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.10 to the tune of Rs.3,307/-.
20.
In this case the petitioner has neither adduced the evidence of doctor nor produced any disability certificate to show that he has become permanently disabled.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income or under any other heads.

Hence,
looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- including the medical expenses.
21. LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-HT-9730 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 31.10.2023 to 30.10.2028.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 12.01.2024.

Hence,
policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
22. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble Manjunatha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 20 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2854192/
5 High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as it is meager.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
